latest_findings.claim: At e<=0.9, the 3000-step layer-4 accel_step R2 settles well below the matched e<=0.85 values in all 3 seeds. Seed 70: 0.457 vs 0.573, gap 0.116. Seed 71: 0.421 vs 0.558, gap 0.137. Seed 72: 0.447 vs 0.588, gap 0.141. accel_step still beats its control (margins 0.305/0.271/0.277, controls 0.15-0.17), and the headroom-normalised margin is 0.360/0.319/0.334, all below 0.40. R2 rose only 0.011-0.064 from the 600-step values (0.393/0.396/0.436) and was flat within about 0.01 from step 1000-2250 onward, while val_mse_ratio kept falling about 10x (about 0.12 to 0.013-0.015). Force also beats its control but is much weaker and less stable than accel_step. Force R2 is 0.310/0.200/0.373, with margins 0.140/0.131/0.212 and normalised margins 0.17/0.14/0.25. Its best layer is 4/1/2 depending on seed, while accel_step peaks at layer 4 in every seed.
latest_findings.confidence_note: All 3 seeds completed the full 3000 steps (none stopped early). All gaps clear the 0.08 bar by at least 0.036, and the margins and normalised margins pass with room to spare, so the verdict does not depend on borderline numbers. Limits: (1) The e<=0.85 reference values come from a different experiment (f-20261013-001616-659c). The comparison assumes the same data_seed, pipeline version and best-of-5 control draw, and if the reference R2 had been read at a different layer or under an older control scheme the gaps could shift by a few hundredths. (2) Only one data_seed and one architecture (d_model=64, 4 layers) were tested, so the 'lower ceiling' is a ceiling for this model and a linear probe. A nonlinear or log(accel_step) probe, or a wider model, could still decode much more. (3) Seed 71 was still gaining about 0.005 per 250 steps at the end, so a longer run might narrow its gap somewhat, though not by the 0.10 needed to reach the 'false' band. The verdict would change if a 6000+ step run brought any seed within 0.04 of its e<=0.85 value, or if matched-layer, same-pipeline e<=0.85 reruns turned out much closer to these values.

latest_findings.claim: At matched 24000-step horizon (m2 = 0.5, data_seed 0, seed 22), N=64 final layer-1 force R2 = 0.80399 (control 0.57407, margin 0.230, best layer 1). That is 0.114 above the same-layer N=128 value of 0.6903 (run-20261015-214139-70d4) and 0.099 above N=128's best layer (layer 3, 0.70462; cross-layer comparison). accel_step R2 = 0.95241 at layer 4 (control 0.72946, headroom-normalised margin 0.82). The pre-registered horizon check failed: layer-1 force at step 12000 of this run is about 0.794-0.796 (control plus margin), which is 0.044 below the 12000-step run's endpoint of 0.8398 (run-20261014-043150-f21c), above the 0.03 tolerance. This run's 24000-step endpoint (0.804) is also 0.036 below that 12000-step endpoint.
latest_findings.confidence_note: Every gap criterion passes by a wide margin. Same-layer gap 0.114 and cross-layer gap 0.099, against the 0.04 bar and the 0.02 refutation line. Force margin 0.230 >= 0.1. accel_step normalised margin 0.82 is inside [0.60, 0.85]. The run completed all 24000 steps. The verdict is inconclusive for one reason: the pre-registered horizon check failed by 0.044, and the hypothesis said that outcome must be reported as horizon-confounded. That failure does not weaken the matched-horizon N=64 vs N=128 comparison, since both runs are 24000 steps. It does show that seed-22 N=64 force depends on the lr schedule. Force peaks at about 0.806 at step 6000, dips to about 0.795 at step 11000, and recovers only to 0.812 (trajectory max) by step 24000, even though val_mse_ratio falls about 8x to 0.00095. Comparisons between the 12000-step and 24000-step runs are therefore not like-for-like. A matched-loss reading points the same way. At steps 12000-13000 (val_mse_ratio 0.008-0.004), N=64 layer-1 force is about 0.796, roughly 0.09 or more above N=128's 0.69-0.70 at a similar loss. Limits: this is one seed on one dataset, intermediate values come from 3-decimal trajectory fields, and the step-12000 value assumes the step-12000 control equals the final layer-1 control (0.57407, the same as the reference run's control). Two things would change the verdict to supported: rerunning the horizon check against a schedule-fraction-matched checkpoint (step 6000 of the 12000-step run versus step 12000 here), or a second seed showing a same-layer gap >= 0.04 at 24000 steps on data_seed 0. A same-layer gap below 0.04 in such a replication would weaken the ceiling interpretation.

latest_findings.claim: With m2 fixed at 0.5 on data_seed 1, the N=64 seed-23 24000-step run ends with force R2 0.84445 at layer 1. Layer 1 is also its best-margin layer, so this is a same-layer comparison. Force control is 0.63224, margin 0.212. The gap to the same-layer 24000-step N=128 seed-23 value (0.81915, run-20261015-225826-a2d5) is 0.025. That falls in the pre-registered inconclusive band (0.02, 0.04): the prediction needed >= 0.859, and the false case was <= 0.839. The horizon check passes: at step 12000, layer-1 control plus margin is about 0.632 + 0.203 = 0.835, within 0.012 of the 12000-step reference run-20261014-074634-b5ab (0.8467). accel_step reaches R2 0.952 at layer 3 vs control 0.769. Its headroom-normalised margin is 0.79, inside the predicted [0.60, 0.85], against 0.58 for force.
latest_findings.confidence_note: This is a single seed on a single dataset. The run completed all 24000 steps. The 0.025 gap sits 0.005 above the 'converges' bound and 0.015 below the 'ceiling' bound, so the verdict depends on noise at about the level of the force control_spread (0.028). N=64 force has levelled off at about 0.845 whatever the horizon: 0.8467 at the end of the 12000-step run and 0.8445 at the end of this one. So the seed-23 gap shrinking from about 0.032 at 12000 steps to 0.025 at 24000 comes entirely from N=128's late gain (+0.008), not from any change on the N=64 side. Inside this run, force was flat from step 3000 to step 12000 (0.831-0.835) and gained about 0.013 only in the second half, which fits a low-lr-tail effect. At matched val_mse_ratio the comparison could shift further, because N=64 reaches 0.0009, far below N=128. The verdict would move to 'refuted' if N=128 seed 23 trained longer (or read at matched loss) closes to within 0.02 of 0.845. It would move to 'supported' only if N=128 levels off at or below 0.805. Seed 22 on data_seed 0 (exp-20261016-004348-f687) is still running and will show whether the large-gap seed behaves differently.

latest_findings.claim: With m2 fixed at 0.5, N=64 seed 21 trained to 24000 steps has layer-1 force R2 0.8401 (control 0.6308, margin 0.209). That is 0.054 above the same-layer, same-horizon N=128 seed-21 value of 0.78595, and layer 1 is also N=64's best-margin layer, so the gap is not cross-layer. accel_step reaches R2 0.963 at layer 4 against a 0.786 control (margin 0.177, headroom-normalised 0.83), so force's margin is the larger one (0.209 vs 0.177), while accel_step has the higher raw and headroom-normalised score.
latest_findings.confidence_note: Single seed on one dataset. The N=128 reference (run-20261015-221819-33a7) is a separate run. The comparison is matched in layer and horizon but not in loss. N=64 ends at val_mse_ratio 0.0011, against about 0.0044 for N=128 seed 21. Reading this run as layer-1 control plus margin near val_mse_ratio 0.004 (steps 14000-16000, R2 0.824-0.828) gives a gap of about 0.038-0.042, which sits right at the 0.04 bar. So the ceiling claim holds at matched horizon but is borderline at matched loss. The horizon check can only be partly verified here. At step 12000 this run's layer-1 force R2 is 0.819, within about 0.011 of the roughly 0.830 best-layer (layer 2) value reported for the 12000-step N=64 run (run-20261014-054942-67f0, not cited because it is outside this experiment). That run's layer-1 value is not in these records, so a strict same-layer horizon check is still pending. N=64 layer-1 force is still rising slowly (about +0.001 per 1000 steps at the end). Over steps 12000-24000 the two arms gained similar amounts (N=64 +0.021 within this run, N=128 +0.020 between endpoints), so the gap looks stable with training rather than closing. The verdict would change if the matched-loss same-layer gap falls clearly below 0.04, or if the other 24000-step references (seed 23 on data_seed 1, seed 22 on data_seed 0) show gaps of 0.02 or less.

latest_findings.claim: At e<=0.9 (N=64, 4 layers, d_model=64, m2 in [0.1, 1], 600 steps, best-of-5 controls), linear decodability of accel_step kept falling in all 3 seeds. Raw layer-4 accel_step R2 was 0.3927/0.3960/0.4361 (seeds 70/71/72), down from 0.557/0.541/0.570 at e<=0.85, and the headroom-normalised margin was 0.284/0.290/0.320. Margins over control stayed well above the bar (0.240/0.246/0.266; controls 0.150-0.170, spread <= 0.014), and accel_step formed at step 100 in every seed. Force was much weaker: margins of 0.103 (layer 2), 0.084 (layer 2, below the 0.1 bar) and 0.144 (layer 1), headroom-normalised 0.12/0.09/0.17. accel_step beat force in every seed, on both raw and normalised margin.
latest_findings.confidence_note: All three predicted conditions held in all 3 seeds by a wide margin (raw R2 is at least 0.08 below the 0.52 cut-off, and normalised margin at least 0.04 below 0.36), so the verdict does not depend on borderline values. Limits: (1) these are 600-step runs and are not converged. val_mse_ratio is still falling (0.14 to 0.12 over steps 500-600) and accel_step margin is still rising by about 0.002-0.005 per 50 steps, so part of the drop from e<=0.85 could be slower convergence on harder data rather than a lower ceiling. (2) Only one data_seed (0) was used. (3) Checkpoints are 50 steps apart, so the step-100 formation step is coarse. (4) The e<=0.85 comparison values come from a separate experiment run under the same config. Over 0.05 of eccentricity, raw R2 fell about 0.13-0.16, steeper than the roughly 0.19 drop seen over 0.10 from e<=0.75 to e<=0.85, which fits a steepening curve. The verdict would change if 3000-step e<=0.9 runs lifted raw R2 back to 0.55 or more, or if a second data_seed gave normalised margins of 0.38 or more.

config.hypothesis: Width replication on data_seed 1. Setup: m2 fixed at 0.5, data_seed 1, e in [0, 0.5], 4 layers, d_model=128, best-of-3 controls, seeds 22-23, 6000 steps. Prediction: the N=128 force deficit persists at twice the width, so final trained force R2 stays at least 0.04 below the same seed's 6000-step d_model=128 N=64 value from the paired arm proposed this cycle, while accel_step decodability is unchanged. Values come from probes_final, unrounded. The headline gap uses the best-margin layer, with the layer reported and cross-layer pairs flagged. A layer-1 same-layer gap is also reported wherever both arms list layer 1. Within-run values are read only as same-layer control plus margin, never from the max-over-layers trajectory field. If the paired N=64 run is unavailable, that seed's gap is reported as not computed.
